title: network.json
description: modify_network output record: the trimmed/tagged/merged reach network that build_model's db_uri subsequently points at. Grounded in jobs/modify_network/nhf_network_mod.py's NHFNetworkModifier (prototype, not yet wrapped as a stateless job) and modify_network_specs.md, the source of truth for field names. No Realization axis — operates on the whole network in one shot, not addressed by reach_id/domain/scenario — so id == identity_hash. See guide.md's Identity/Realization pattern (this is the Identity-only variant) and the shared envelope in guide.md#manifest.

created_at.description: Write completion time (UTC). network.json is written last, after network.gpkg/lakes.gpkg.

id.description: Equal to identity_hash — no realization code to append. See description above.

identity.description: The inputs that define Network identity; hashed to identity_hash. A change to any of these should fork identity_hash and force a rebuild — transitively forcing every downstream Model to notice via reach_geom_hash once it re-reads reach_network_path. Naming rule: every dataset member is its inputs counterpart with the _path suffix replaced by _hash (inputs.lakes_layer_path -> identity.lakes_layer_hash), so the mapping is mechanical and stays in step when an input is renamed. Threshold members carry the same name in both objects, holding the resolved value after defaults are applied — inputs records the call verbatim and may be null there.

reach_network_hash.description: Hash of the raw hydrofabric network source + version read from inputs.reach_network_path (NHFNetworkModifier.reach_network_path connection params).

lakes_layer_hash.description: Hash of the lakes source + version read from inputs.lakes_layer_path (NHF v1.2.3 lakes_polygons layer — not a pre-built dead-pool dataset; the dead-pool extent is derived at runtime via negative_lake_buffer_meters, see DR-034). Null when no lakes dataset was supplied and lake processing was skipped — required-but-nullable so 'no lakes' is stated explicitly rather than by omission, which would otherwise hash differently.

coastal_influence_layer_hash.description: Hash of the coastal/tidal-influence surface vector source + version read from inputs.coastal_influence_layer_path (DR-038). Null when no coastal dataset was supplied and coastal processing was skipped.

drainage_area_threshold_percent.description: Max difference in total_da_sqkm (cumulative drainage area, %) between reaches eligible for merge; measured against the chain start, not the immediate neighbor. Code default 5 (DR-024).

stream_order_filter_threshold.description: Minimum Strahler stream order kept in the network at all — reaches below this are filtered out entirely, at load time, before lake/coastal/merge processing. No default: when omitted the filter is not applied at all and every reach in reach_network_path enters processing, recorded here as null. Required-but-nullable so 'unfiltered' is stated explicitly rather than by omission, which would otherwise hash differently.

min_length_threshold_km.description: Minimum length (km) a reach should reach by merging — a floor, not a ceiling. Merging continues until the chain clears it, then stops, so a merged reach is bounded at this value plus the single reach that crossed it. A reach already at or above it never merges. Default 5 (DR-024, revised from 3 when the rule changed from ceiling to floor).

lake_area_threshold_sqkm.description: Minimum lake area (km2) to be considered at all; smaller waterbodies are dropped before reach classification. Code default 5. Not present in DR-007/DR-034 text — a code-only parameter.

negative_lake_buffer_meters.description: Inward buffer (m) applied to raw lake polygons to approximate the dead-pool extent. Code default 50. This is the actual mechanism behind DR-034 ALT-A ('shrink an existing waterbody dataset') — not a separately-sourced dead-pool dataset.

inputs.description: The modify_network call arguments, recorded verbatim. This is Network's provenance — not part of identity_hash.

reach_network_path.description: Path to the raw input hydrofabric reach network. Must be a GPKG file; column/layer names follow the NHF v1.2.3 flowpaths layer schema by default. Maps to NHFNetworkModifier.reach_network_path.

lakes_layer_path.description: Path to the lakes dataset. Must be a GPKG file; column/layer names follow the NHF v1.2.3 lakes_polygons layer schema by default. Optional — when absent, lake processing is skipped entirely (no reaches encompassed, trimmed, or split on lakes) and no lakes asset is written. Maps to NHFNetworkModifier.lakes_layer_path.

coastal_influence_layer_path.description: Path to the coastal/tidal-influence surface boundary as a vector dataset. Must be a GPKG file; default layer name is coastal_influence. Optional — when absent, coastal processing is skipped entirely (no reaches dropped, trimmed, or cascade-dropped on coasts). Maps to NHFNetworkModifier.coastal_influence_layer_path.

base_output_path.description: Path where the modified network and manifest are written.

stream_order_filter_threshold.description: Minimum Strahler stream order to keep. Optional — when absent or null, no stream-order filtering is applied and every reach enters processing.

properties.description: Computed/diagnostic values; informational, not part of identity. One counter per real processing branch, so a run is auditable against the code path it took. Null and 0 are distinct: 0 means the branch ran and matched nothing, null means the branch did not run — so every lake counter is null when lakes_layer_path was absent, and every coastal counter is null when coastal_influence_layer_path was absent. The removal counters are disjoint — every reach is counted in exactly one, the branch that removed it, and a reach flagged by both coastal and lake logic (the ambiguous_reach_classification case) is attributed to coastal because step 4 runs before step 5. That disjointness is what lets the counters reconcile: n_reaches_output = n_reaches_input - n_reaches_below_stream_order_removed - n_reaches_encompassed_removed_lake - n_reaches_encompassed_removed_coastal - n_reaches_dropped_coastal_cascade - n_reaches_orphaned_lake - n_reaches_merged + n_reaches_split_passthrough_lake. The trim counters are absent from that identity by design (trimming reshapes a reach and keeps its row); splits add a row each. JSON Schema cannot express this constraint, so it must be enforced by the producer.

n_reaches_input.description: Rows in reach_network_path as read, before the stream-order filter and before any other processing.

n_reaches_below_stream_order_removed.description: Dropped by the stream_order_filter_threshold filter before any waterbody/merge processing. Null when no threshold was given and the filter did not run, in which case the term drops out of the reconciliation identity above.

n_reaches_encompassed_removed_lake.description: Fully inside a lake polygon — classified as encompassed and dropped. The classification is intermediate: every reach it applies to is removed, so it leaves no column in network.gpkg. See assets.network for the columns that do persist.

n_reaches_encompassed_removed_coastal.description: Made first contact with coastal coverage at its upstream end — fully inside, or beginning inside and running back out, or both ends inside while crossing an island. Nothing of the reach lies above the coastline, so it is dropped whole, as is everything downstream of it (counted separately under n_reaches_dropped_coastal_cascade). The classification is intermediate: every reach it applies to is removed, so it leaves no column in network.gpkg.

n_reaches_trimmed_inlet_lake.description: Downstream end inside a lake — trimmed to upstream portion, is_terminal set.

n_reaches_trimmed_outlet_lake.description: Upstream end inside a lake — trimmed to downstream portion, is_headwater set.

n_reaches_trimmed_coastal.description: Began outside coastal coverage and was trimmed at its first contact, keeping the portion above it, terminal_reason='coast'. Covers both a reach whose downstream end is inside and one that passes through with neither end inside. Row kept, so absent from the reconciliation identity.

n_reaches_dropped_coastal_cascade.description: Removed for being downstream of a coastal encompassed/trimmed reach, not for their own classification.

n_reaches_stranded_coastal.description: Tributaries left pointing at a cascade-deleted reach without themselves intersecting the coast layer — made terminal (terminal_reason='coast', reach_to_id nulled), geometry untouched. Not removed, so absent from the reconciliation identity.

n_reaches_split_passthrough_lake.description: Passed through a lake at both ends outside it — split into a new inlet/outlet reach pair, minting a new reach_id.

n_reaches_trimmed_between_lakes.description: Started inside one lake and ended inside another — trimmed at both ends, keeping the dry middle as a channel between the two. The inverse of a pass-through split, which keeps the ends and drops the middle. The survivor is both lake_outlet and lake_inlet, and both headwater and terminal. Row kept, so it is absent from the reconciliation identity. lake_to_id names the downstream lake.

n_reaches_orphaned_lake.description: Left with no upstream and no downstream once lake removal took both neighbors, and not an original headwater. The shape is a reach crossing an island inside a lake: trimmed to the island width as an inlet, with the water on both sides encompassed and dropped. Removed, so it enters the reconciliation identity. Lake outlets and genuine one-reach watersheds are never swept, because both are headwaters.

n_reaches_merged.description: Consumed by a drainage-area-difference merge into a downstream neighbor.

n_reaches_output.description: Rows in the written network.gpkg, after every step including merge. The left-hand side of the reconciliation identity above.

n_headwater_reaches.description: Rows in the written network.gpkg with is_headwater true — a state of the final artifact, NOT a count of any one step. Measured after all trimming, splitting, and merging. A headwater is a reach that is no other reach's fp_to_id, i.e. nothing flows into it. Two steps set this flag: step 3 (topological headwaters) and step 5 (lake outlets, also counted by n_reaches_trimmed_outlet_lake), so this exceeds step 3's own tally. Expect this to be large relative to n_reaches_output whenever stream_order_filter_threshold is set — the filter strands every reach whose feeders were below the threshold, making them apparent headwaters. A consumer can verify it by opening network.gpkg and counting; that is the definition.

n_terminal_reaches.description: Rows in the written network.gpkg with is_terminal true — a state of the final artifact, NOT a count of any one step. Measured after all trimming, splitting, and merging. Three steps set this flag: step 2 (outlets), step 4 (coastal inlets, counted by n_reaches_trimmed_coastal, plus stranded tributaries, counted by n_reaches_stranded_coastal) and step 5 (lake inlets, counted by n_reaches_trimmed_inlet_lake), so this exceeds step 2's own tally. Can overlap n_headwater_reaches — an isolated reach with neither an upstream nor a downstream neighbor is both — so the two are not additive and neither appears in the reconciliation identity. The overlap is incidental, not systematic: headwater and terminal are independent topological ends.

assets.description: This job's own outputs, written as separate GeoPackage files under base_output_path. network.gpkg is always present; lakes.gpkg only when lake processing ran, which is why only 'network' is required.

network.description: The modified reach network, written as the reach_network layer — the table name build_model queries through its db_uri (the input NHF layer is flowpaths; the output deliberately differs). Output columns are a closed set; every source column outside it is dropped, including fp_id/fp_to_id, which reach_id/reach_to_id supersede. Identity: reach_id, reach_to_id — both TEXT. A divided reach retires its id and suffixes every piece: a multipart geometry explodes to 3434_1/3434_2/3434_3, a lake split gives 8_1/8_2, and the two nest as 3434_3_1. Pointers into a divided reach are repointed at its first/upstream piece. Geometry is always LineString; multipart input is exploded at load. Waterbody references: lake_to_id (the lake layer's lake_id), coast_to_id (the coastal layer's id), null where the reach never met one — a stranded reach has terminal_reason coast but a null coast_to_id. Tags: is_headwater, is_terminal, terminal_reason (one of outlet, coast, lake, or null when is_terminal is false; no separate coastal inlet/outlet/encompassed columns), lake_inlet, lake_outlet, is_trimmed (true where geometry was cut, false for stranded). For build_model: stream_order and total_da_sqkm carried through from the source; length_km recomputed from the final geometry for every reach, so every row is verifiable against the artifact and trimmed, split, merged and untouched reaches all share one measure. A source length_km is neither required nor preserved. area_sqkm (local catchment) is not carried. These are the literal GPKG column names.

lakes.description: The filtered (lake_area_threshold_sqkm) and buffered (negative_lake_buffer_meters) lake polygons actually used for classification — kept for QC/reference, not itself part of the reach network (DR-037 ALT-B: lakes are not inserted as network reaches). Present only when inputs.lakes_layer_path was supplied; absent when lake processing was skipped, which is why only 'network' is required.

warnings.description: Non-fatal check results recorded in the network.json this run writes. Only ambiguous_reach_classification can appear here: the job completes and persists it. network_exists is a response-only warning — it short-circuits before any processing or write, so it is returned to the caller alongside the pre-existing identity_hash and never lands in a persisted manifest. It stays in the enum to keep one warning vocabulary.

href.description: Path to the file, e.g. network.gpkg, lakes.gpkg, or a full s3:// URI.

checksum.description: File-integrity checksum; longer than identity hashes to allow cross-corpus content comparison.

source_url.description: External provenance URL, if applicable. Null for purely computed assets — both of this job's assets are computed, so both are null.

retrieved.description: When the source was fetched, if applicable. Never set for this job's assets, which are computed rather than fetched.

derived.description: True for outputs regenerable from sources; subject to S3 lifecycle deletion. Always false for this job — nothing it writes is disposable. Both assets are regenerable in principle, but network.gpkg is what build_model's db_uri points at and lakes.gpkg is retained for QC, so neither is lifecycle-eligible. State it explicitly on every asset rather than relying on this default, so retention is a recorded decision.
